title: TTP-S Protocol for Mouse Brain Tissue Preparation and Analysis
author: Evan J. Kyzar
materials: Brains are removed from sucrose and dried using a Kimwipe prior to embedding in OCT in a brain mold (e.g,. Peel-A-Way molds; Sigma-Aldrich) and flash freezing in a 100% EtOH solution with dry ice. Brains can be stored at -80°C until IHC is performed.

Incubate with primary antibodies dissolved in blocking solution (see step 10 above) overnight (~18 hrs) on shaker at 4°C. We recommend the primary antibody from Cell Signaling (#2250S; 1:1000 dilution) and the NeuN antibody from EMD Millpore (#MAB377; 1:1000 dilution). Note that our protocol can be adapted for use with other primary and secondary antibodies.

Incubate with secondary antibodies for 2 hrs on shaker at room temperature. We recommend the Invitrogen donkey anti-rabbit AF647 (#A31573; 1:1000 dilution) and the Life Technologies donkey anti-mouse AF488 (#A21202; 1:1000 dilution), as well as a DAPI stain (e.g., Sigma Aldrich #D9542; 1:5000 dilution).

steps.title: Animal Habituation and Grouping
steps.instruction: Prepare Trap2:Ai14 mice (n≥5 per group) by exposing them to discrete stimuli. Habituate mice to injection stress with sham i.p. injections for at least 3 days prior to Timepoint 1 (TP1). If using a subtraction procedure, include a subtraction group exposed to homecage conditions at both TP1 and TP2, or different stimuli at each timepoint.

steps.title: Timepoint 1 (TP1) Administration
steps.instruction: Administer 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) to mice at a dose of 50mg/kg.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 4-OHT in 100% ethanol to a concentration of 20mg/mL.
Mix the 4-OHT solution with an equal volume of a 1:4 mixture of castor oil:sunflower oil.
Vacuum centrifuge the mixture at 43°C for 45min.
Inject each mouse with 50mg/kg of 4-OHT.
Maintain mice in social isolation and a dark environment following stimulus exposure and administration to minimize non-stimulus-related activity.

steps.title: Timepoint 2 (TP2) and Sacrifice
steps.instruction: Expose mice to the same stimulus at least 7 days after TP1 (or sooner if using anti-tdTomato antibody to boost red channel signal), then sacrifice for c-Fos labeling.

steps.title: Tissue Fixation and Sectioning
steps.instruction: Perform transcardial perfusion and prepare brain sections.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mice (e.g., ketamine/xylazine) and transcardially perfuse with 20mL PBS followed by 20mL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Remove brain and post-fix in 4% PFA overnight at 4°C.
Transfer brains to 20% sucrose in PBS at 4°C until the brain sinks (typically 24-36 hours). Note: This step can be skipped if using a vibratome.
Slice brains coronally at 50 micron thickness using a cryostat (for frozen tissue) or vibratome.

steps.title: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) Staining
steps.instruction: Process brain sections through washing, blocking, and mounting.

substeps.instruction: Wash sections 3x in cold PBS for 5 min each.
Block with 5% normal donkey serum in PBST (3% Triton in PBS) for 1 hr on a shaker at room temperature.
Wash sections 3x in PBST for 5 min each.
Wash sections 3x in PBS for 5 min each.
Mount 6-8 sections per microscope slide.
Allow coverslipped sections to dry for at least 24 hours prior to imaging.

steps.title: Confocal Imaging
steps.instruction: Capture tiled images of each brain slice at 4x magnification using a high-sensitivity confocal microscope (e.g., W1-Yokogawa inverted spinning disk).

substeps.instruction: DAPI: 405nm wavelength (100% laser power, 50ms exposure).
NeuN: 488nm wavelength (100%, 100ms).
tdTomato: 568nm wavelength (100%, 100ms).
cFos: 647nm wavelength (100%, 300ms).

steps.title: Image Renaming and Organization
steps.instruction: Use Advanced Renamer to sequentially order brain slice images.

substeps.instruction: Set 'Renumber' method: Number position 1, Absolute number, New number 01, Skip 1, Zero padding Automatic.
Set 'Add' method: Add 0 at index 1.
Process folders of slides sequentially, updating the 'New number' to follow the previous batch (e.g., if the last file was 032, start the next batch at 033).
When file names reach triple digits, remove the '0' from the 'Add' tab to maintain three-digit formatting (e.g., 120).
Place all renamed files into a single folder labeled 'BrainJ'.

steps.title: BrainJ Registration Setup
steps.instruction: Configure experimental parameters in ImageJ using the BrainJ plugin.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to Plugins > BrainJ > 1 Set Experiment Parameters.

Set: Analysis type (Whole brain), Sample type (Mouse brain: Coronal Sections), Input image type (2D Slices), Rotation/Flipping (No), File order (Alphanumeric), Order of sections (Right), Lateral resolution (1.615 um), Final resolution (1.615 um/px), and input section thickness.
Input counterstain channel (DAPI) and background intensity (average of blank space, typically ~98).
Check 'Perform automatic tissue detection' and click OK.
Navigate to Plugins > BrainJ > 2 Reformat sections, set Threshold method to 'Mean', and click OK.

steps.title: Section Quality Control and Correction
steps.instruction: Review and correct section orientation and damage in ImageJ.

substeps.instruction: Drag 'Section Preview Stack' from the '2_Section Preview' folder into ImageJ; adjust Brightness/Contrast if necessary.
Identify sections requiring flipping or replacement.

Navigate to Plugins > BrainJ > 3 Section Flipper and Replacer; enter section numbers for horizontal flipping, vertical flipping, and replacement (Method: Replace DAPI/registration channel, clear others).
Use the Circle shape tool to draw a tight circle around each section. If needed, use ImageJ > Transform > Rotate to straighten the section.

steps.title: Atlas Registration and Analysis
steps.instruction: Register the brain sections to the Allen Brain Atlas (ABA).

substeps.instruction: Navigate to Plugins > BrainJ > 4_Set Analysis Settings. Select the BrainJ folder and a reference section (undamaged section near the middle of the stack).
Set Background removal to 7, check 'Generate full resolution registered image of reference channel' and 'Perform a second pass section registration'.
Set Cell Analysis and Mesoscale Mapping to 'No Analysis'. Ensure Ilastik and Elastix paths are correct.
Navigate to Plugins > BrainJ > 5 Registration and Atlas Analysis. Set the ABA registration file path, check 'Perform section registration' and 'Perform atlas registration'.
Review alignment by dragging 'Template brain aligned' from the '5_Analysis_Output' folder into ImageJ.

steps.title: Post-Registration Data Processing
steps.instruction: Transfer registered data to an analysis computer and run the BrainJ-Python pipeline.

substeps.instruction: Move folders '3_Registered_Sections', '4_Processed_Sections', '5_Analysis_Output', 'Ilastik_Projects', and 'Analysis_Settings.csv' to the analysis computer.
Ensure the computer has the ABA Common Coordinate Framework, Elastix v5.0.1, BrainJ-Python extension, and appropriate restoration/segmentation models.
Copy 'Analysis_Settings.yaml' to the brain output folder and update the reference section.
Update the file path in 'BrainJ_Batch_script_template.py' and run the script (requires high-performance computing, e.g., 16GB RAM, NVIDIA GPU).

steps.title: Statistical Analysis and Cell Counting
steps.instruction: Process cell counts and perform statistical inference using MATLAB.

substeps.instruction: Run 'TTP_combine_hemispheres.m' on the Cell_Analysis folder. Use 'useMask=true' for adaptive-mask sensitivity (published analyses use _MinMask).
Create a batch spreadsheet and run 'Batch_Load_Data_BrainJ_Both_Hemi_Working.m' to load data into MATLAB workspace variables.
Optional: Use the brain area collapse extension to group ABA regions.

Run 'TTPS_pval_loop.m' to compare two groups (e.g., group AA vs subtraction group AB) and generate a p-values CSV. Default settings: 300 hypergeometric draws, alpha 0.05, Bonferroni divisor 500. Published analyses use the Harmonic p-value.
Optional: Perform graph theoretical analysis using the Brain Connectivity Toolbox.

description: Download .ijm file entitled "Background_subtraction_looped new.ijm" from Github. Link to download here: https://github.com/ekyzar/ttps_pipeline/tree/main/background_subtraction Drag it to ImageJ > Run > navigate to BrainJ folder of brain in progress > "1_Reformatted Sections" > select folder representing the counterstain channel. A window with the sections will appear.
